title: The Battle of Thermopylae
shortDesc: Three hundred Spartans and their allies hold a pass against Persia.

title: Victory in Europe Day
shortDesc: Germany surrenders and crowds celebrate across the Allied world.
fullDesc: On May 8, 1945 the Allies celebrated the formal surrender of Nazi Germany, a week after Hitler's death. Huge crowds filled the streets in London, Paris and New York, though the war with Japan continued until August.
realFacts: Princess Elizabeth slipped out into the London crowds
Germany signed at Reims and again in Berlin
More than 60 million people died in the war
Russia marks Victory Day on May 9

title: The Nuremberg Trials Begin
shortDesc: Nazi leaders are tried for war crimes before an international court.
fullDesc: From November 1945 the main Nazi leaders were tried at Nuremberg by judges from the US, Britain, France and the Soviet Union. Twelve were sentenced to death. The trials set precedents for international law on war crimes and crimes against humanity.
realFacts: Hermann Göring killed himself before execution
Some defendants were acquitted
The concept of crimes against humanity was developed
It led to later tribunals in places like Rwanda and Yugoslavia
